note: Every registry event is written from one template. The entry is written on the asset (drug, device, program, rule), never on the corporate name, so mergers and renames do not void it. 'A and B' splits into two events; 'A or B' is one event. The same entry resolves every forecaster's items.

templates.criterion: TRUE on the date the regulator's approval letter or database entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) is dated. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote or a filing acceptance is not an approval. A label narrower than the indication named in the claim counts if the claim's indication reasonably includes it and the reading is logged at intake.
templates.source: Drugs@FDA or the regulator's database; sponsor press release as a secondary source.

templates.proposition: <Regulator> grants <clearance, De Novo, PMA or breakthrough designation> for <device> for <indication>.
templates.criterion: TRUE on the decision date in the regulator's database (510(k), De Novo, PMA) or the sponsor's announcement of a designation. Intended-use and setting (home use, clinic) must match the claim.
templates.source: FDA 510(k), De Novo or PMA database; sponsor release for designations.

templates.proposition: <Program> reports <primary endpoint met or not met> in <trial> (or <effect size threshold>).
templates.criterion: TRUE on the date of the sponsor's topline release or the publication that first reports the result. 'Positive' means the prespecified primary endpoint met significance as reported by the sponsor; an effect-size threshold in the claim is resolved on the reported estimate.
templates.source: Sponsor topline press release; ClinicalTrials.gov results; peer-reviewed publication.

templates.proposition: <Body> adopts, extends, rescinds or issues <rule, guidance, order, law or program>.
templates.criterion: TRUE on the publication date in the Federal Register, the agency site, the state register or the enacted bill's effective or signing date as named in the claim. A proposal is not adoption unless the claim was about the proposal.
templates.source: Federal Register; agency press release; state legislature record.

templates.proposition: <Court or agency> <convicts, sentences, rules, dismisses or settles> in <case>.
templates.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the verdict, sentence, order or filed settlement named in the claim.
templates.source: Court docket (CourtListener, PACER), DOJ press release.

templates.proposition: <Company or program> <is acquired, files for bankruptcy, lays off staff, raises, lists, delists, shuts down, launches a product, or misses or hits a number>.
templates.criterion: TRUE on the date of the definitive public announcement (SEC filing, press release, court filing) of the event named in the claim; rumors and letters of intent do not count unless the claim was about them.
templates.source: SEC EDGAR; company press release; bankruptcy docket.

templates.proposition: <Payer or program> covers, stops covering, or changes payment for <treatment or code>.
templates.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of the published coverage policy, fee schedule, NCD or LCD, or the payer's public policy bulletin named in the claim.
templates.source: CMS Medicare Coverage Database; payer policy bulletins; Federal Register fee schedule.

templates.proposition: <Metric> is at or beyond <threshold> (or moves in <direction>) by <period end>, per <named series>.
templates.criterion: Resolved on the named data series only. A direction resolves as binary at the threshold in the forecaster's words. A bare point number takes a fixed band of plus or minus 20 percent. If the series has not published 12 months after the deadline, the event is unresolvable. Realized values are stored, not scored.
templates.source: The named public series (IQVIA, SEC filings, FDA database counts, a named investment tracker).
